findings.title: The guard docblock re-asserts a mutation-testing result that is false for two of its three guards — and this branch’s own new test is what falsified one of them
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The rewritten docblock states: "Branch review round 1 mutation-tested the original three: deleting guard 1, 2 or 3 individually changes no outcome and kills no test, because the resolver guard already covers each case." The branch did not merely leave this sentence alone — it renumbered it, and then explicitly bounded the staleness risk to guard 4 ("THAT RESULT IS ABOUT THOSE THREE AND THE RESOLVER GUARD (now numbered 5) AND NOTHING ELSE — guard 4 post-dates it (#1079)"). That re-scoping publishes the claim as CURRENT at 659810f2. Three individual mutations measured at HEAD: guard 1 deleted (M10) KILLS the branch’s own new test T7, "the held_draft lane still writes its refusal row…", because that test’s `expect(resolvePolicyGateRefusalSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` did not exist when round 1 measured — the same commit that re-asserts the claim is the commit that falsifies it. Guard 3 deleted (M12) KILLS the pre-existing "a structural non-candidate draft writes no policy_gate_held row" AND changes the OUTCOME: a policy_gate_held row is written ("expected [ { …(9) } ] to have a length of +0 but got 1"), so both halves of the sentence fail there; that half was already false at the fork point f797d250 (the test predates the branch) and is re-published rather than introduced. Guard 2 deleted (M11) SURVIVES 82/82 — the claim holds for exactly one of the three. This is not an equivalent-mutant question and not a style objection: the docblock’s stated purpose is to tell the next reader which guards are safe to remove, and it currently licenses removing guard 3, which would write a spurious Refusal row for a structural non-candidate — a data-correctness defect in the ledger the Restraint tab renders. Classified P0 under the skill’s "a misleading FALSE claim is P0", and because the branch holds itself to precisely this standard three lines later ("an earlier version of this docblock claimed 'each answers a different question', which was false and is corrected here rather than left to mislead the next reader"). No runtime behaviour is wrong; the fix is a docblock correction naming which guard is actually unpinned and which two are now pinned, and by what.

findings.title: The alerting runbook’s refusal-ledger rule row is contradicted on its threshold/cadence facet, and still calls the warning the ledger’s only gap detector
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Six-facet comparison of the documented rule against the signal emitted at 659810f2. Signal identity: MATCHES (captureMessage, tags.subsystem=refusal_ledger via warnLedgerDisabled). Filter: MATCHES, with a pre-existing ambiguity not added here — withLedgerAttribution also tags subsystem=refusal_ledger at level error, and its capture body is unchanged by this diff (only its docblock moved), so this diff adds no new operator-actionable terminal path, it widens an existing one. Level: MATCHES. Grouping title: n/a. Threshold/cadence: CONTRADICTED — the row says the warning fires "once per disabled episode whenever REFUSAL_LEDGER_ENABLED=false and a write is attempted", but guard 4 now returns before any write is attempted on the policy_gate_held lane, so with the flag off that lane contributes nothing to the episode. Destination action: MATCHES. The branch itself records this as an accepted cost in three places (intake observability[3], the arch-review-log row, and the persist.ts guard-4 docblock), and I verified the compensating claim is TRUE: the held_draft lane at persist.ts:930 and all six other production write sites still call writeRefusalEvent(s) with no flag guard, so they still warn. What is missing is the runbook — the operator-facing document that specifies the alert rule and asserts in bold "This is the only signal that the ledger has a gap". It now overstates that coverage with no mention of the blind spot. Scope note for the adjudicator: docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md is NOT in the intake’s allowed_edit_surface, so this is a scope decision for the root rather than an implementer miss; the fix is one sentence.

findings.title: The new file-global auto-approval mock leaves a dictated gate verdict in module state that only the last describe block resets
findings.arbiter_reasoning: vi.mock('../auto-approval') is now file-global in persist.test.ts and consults the module-level mutable `gateOverride`, which is reset to null only in the afterEach of the `invariants` describe at line 1031. That is correct today for exactly one structural reason — `invariants` is the last describe in the file — and the 65/65 green unit baseline confirms no current leakage. It is a latent hazard rather than a present defect: a describe added after `invariants`, or a reorder, would inherit a dictated `approved: false` plus a generated blockReasons array into unrelated cases, and the failure would surface far from its cause (the file’s own queuePersistRows comment already documents how an off-by-one in the tx queue resurfaces as an unrelated tier error). Recorded as P2, non-blocking; a top-level beforeEach resetting gateOverride, or moving the state into the describe, closes it. Not classified as a fragile assertion under Duty 2’s three named shapes — I searched for those specifically and found none: every absence assertion added by this diff carries a proven positive control (T1 by T2, killed under M2; T6 by its trailing non-empty batch, killed under M5 and M6; T5 by its resetRefusalLedgerWarningForTests new-episode arm, killed under M9; T7 killed under M10), the single order assertion (toEqual on the resolver argument in T8) has an explicit ordering contract in vocabulary.ts and is killed under M8, tags are compared with toMatchObject rather than exact equality, and ALL_BLOCK_REASONS is derived via Object.keys rather than hardcoded (its "22 today" comment verified accurate: 15 mapped + 7 null).
